subject: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, SLA targets & routing options
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, SLA targets & routing options

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed action map so we keep momentum: 

Key pain points you shared
- Multi-tenant latency variance when we scale past 2k TPS (esp. 99th pct spikes)
- Regulatory constraint: PHI must remain in a private VPC for inference (no shared prefix cache)
- Cost predictability for peak campaign windows (monthly budget caps)

Goals you want to hit
- Stable 99th percentile latency <= 180 ms for text-gen endpoints at 1.5k QPS sustained
- Photo/medical document uploads routed to isolated private pool for PHI processing
- Procurement-friendly pricing with a 3-month pilot and a clear ramp schedule

What we propose (high level)
- Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) with tenant isolation lanes for PHI paths
- SLA targets: 99th <= 180 ms for standard pool, 99th <= 120 ms for isolated PHI pool (initial target)
- Routing policy: region-first then SLA tier; on overload fallback to quantized cheaper model variant
- Autoscale buckets that prioritize isolation requirements during burst windows

Attached: mutual action plan (MAP) draft and preliminary SLA doc. Please review items highlighted in column B of the MAP — those are your asks we marked as high priority.

Next steps (proposed)
1) You confirm PHI dataset scope for isolation (what endpoints, approximate token sizes) — Alex
2) We provide a short ops appendix with kernel/quantization choices and an expected cost delta for isolated pools — Ben + Priyom (by Mon 20th)
3) Procurement to confirm preferred contract term and PO process — Procurement

If that matches your read, can we lock a 30-min follow-up on Mon 20th at 10am PT to walk procurement through the MAP? 

Thanks — appreciate the clear signals today.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: isolation constraints, SLA targets & routing options

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. That aligns with our read. Quick answers: 
- PHI scope: mainly clinical notes + uploaded images for our triage model; expect average request payload ~3–5 KB, occasionally up to 120 KB for multi-image uploads.
- Priority endpoints: /v1/triage/text-gen and /v1/triage/image-embed (image processing must land in isolated pool)
- Procurement note: we prefer a 3-month pilot with monthly billing and an option to convert to a 12-mo commit. I'll loop procurement on the follow-up.

I can do Mon 20th 10am PT. Adding Procurement on this thread.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of ML Platforms | Medsprint AI
alex.kim@medsprint.ai

Vanessa / Priyom —

Couple of operational clarifications we should confirm before the Monday call so we can have the right tech people on: 
- What token length distribution do they expect for triage text-gen (p50/p95/p99)? Alex gave avg payload but we need token distribution to size KV cache and KV shard mapping.
- For image processing, confirm whether images are pre-processed client-side (base64) or uploaded to S3 with a signed URL; this affects our prefetched-kv strategy.
- Do they need guaranteed cold-start latency (we currently offer warm lane pre-warmed on Dedicated pools as an add-on)? If yes, we'll include warm-lane sizing options in the ops appendix.

I can draft the ops appendix (kernel choices, expected quantization impact, warm-lane sizing) and Fred (ops) can join the call if we can get answers to the above today. Priyom, can you take the lead on cost delta estimates for isolated pool vs shared?
